differences: Collections, people, and search use isolated cards on the page canvas instead of a single bounded Intercom-style workspace with header, controls, and divider rows.
The collection and person detail flows separate review actions from their source lists rather than presenting one continuous operational surface.
Album detail has the correct primary and secondary information but its header, tracks, pressings, and history still read as independent dashboard cards.
Search results use a two-column card grid that reduces scan speed and differs from the dense full-width result rows in the approved reference system.
Narrow layouts preserve function but retain desktop card framing and inconsistent section order.
suggestions: Wrap each route in one rounded workspace surface with a compact header and divider-based internal sections.
Render collections, people, and search results as dense shared rows with stable trailing status and actions.
Use a primary-pane and inspector layout for album detail, keeping tracks first and pressings/history in the inspector.
Keep segmented controls neutral and move selection/action controls into sticky or bounded toolbars.
Collapse the same structures into one primary-first column on phone widths without changing data or actions.
reasoning: These routes already expose the correct real data, permission checks, review steps, pagination, and error states. The gap is local visual hierarchy: they need the same calm workspace surface, shared dividers, dense rows, and stable action placement now used by the main media details.
